parsed.use_case: Low-level arithmetic routines can compute totals on processors or virtual machines where addition must be expressed through primitive bit operations, such as implementing an instruction emulator or a constrained arithmetic library. The same logic is also useful in coding exercises that model how signed integer addition works at the bit level.
system_examples: CPU instruction emulators — implement integer addition according to the emulated instruction set’s carry and overflow behavior.
Cryptographic and embedded arithmetic libraries — perform fixed-width integer operations using bit-level primitives when the target environment constrains available arithmetic instructions.
parsed.explanation: The standard method repeatedly combines XOR for the sum bits without carries and AND followed by a left shift for the carry bits, stopping when no carry remains. It takes O(w) time and O(1) space for a w-bit integer, compared with treating each unit increment as a separate operation; this is mainly a teaching exercise, with direct production use in low-level arithmetic and emulation.
